item.text:
Using the local prior as the structured baseline, I did not re-fetch the country-year datasets you already supplied. I only added narrative / attribution sources and a short event map, with no scoring.

**Office, Authority, Constraints**
- AMLO was president of Mexico in 2022, having taken office on **1 December 2018**. Source: the official presidential inauguration record.
- His formal executive authority was broad: promulgate and execute laws, appoint and remove cabinet officials, direct foreign policy, and exercise command over the armed forces.
- In practice, he was constrained by Congress, the Supreme Court, the National Electoral Institute (INE), federal-state fragmentation, organized-crime violence, inflation/pandemic aftershocks, and a large gap between formal control and policy passage.

**Retained Source Families**
1. [Andrés Manuel López Obrador rinde protesta como Presidente Constitucional de México](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/andres-manuel-lopez-obrador-rinde-protesta-como-presidente-constitucional-de-mexico/) | Presidencia de la República | 1 December 2018  
   - Precise fact: establishes AMLO as constitutional president, which anchors the 2022 office continuity.
   - Period fit: direct office confirmation, even though the publication predates 2022.
   - Ruler attribution: direct.
   - Limitations: inauguration record, not a 2022 performance source.
   - Contrary points: does not address later constraints or governance outcomes.

2. [Artículo 89 de la Constitución Política de los Estados Unidos Mexicanos](https://www.ordenjuridico.gob.mx/Documentos/Federal/html/wo14166.html) | Orden Jurídico / constitutional text in force in 2022  
   - Precise fact: presidential powers include executing laws, appointing/removing senior officials, and command over the armed forces.
   - Period fit: strong for office authority and institutional limits.
   - Ruler attribution: indirect but foundational.
   - Limitations: legal framework, not narrative context.
   - Contrary points: formal powers do not imply effective control over legislature, courts, or security outcomes.

3. [Realiza INE declaratoria de resultados del proceso de Revocación de Mandato](https://centralelectoral.ine.mx/2022/04/11/realiza-ine-declaratoria-de-resultados-del-proceso-de-revocacion-de-mandato/) | INE | 11 April 2022  
   - Precise fact: 17.77% turnout; 91.86% voted to keep AMLO; result was below the 40% threshold and therefore nonbinding.
   - Period fit: one of the key 2022 legitimacy/constraint events.
   - Ruler attribution: direct, because the referendum was about AMLO.
   - Limitations: plebiscitary snapshot, not a general approval measure.
   - Contrary points: low participation limits claims of a broad mandate.

4. [Decreto por el que se reforman... en Materia de Guardia Nacional y Seguridad Pública](https://www.dof.gob.mx/nota_detalle_popup.php?codigo=5702418) | Diario Oficial de la Federación | 9 September 2022  
   - Precise fact: operational and administrative control of the Guardia Nacional was moved to SEDENA.
   - Period fit: central for Chapter 2B and 8B security-state context.
   - Ruler attribution: direct policy choice of the AMLO government.
   - Limitations: legal text; implementation and effects require corroboration.
   - Contrary points: supporters framed it as professionalization; critics as civilian-control erosion.

5. [IMF Executive Board Concludes 2022 Article IV Consultation with Mexico](https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2022/11/04/pr22373-imf-executive-board-concludes-2022-article-iv-consultation-with-mexico) | IMF | 4 November 2022  
   - Precise fact: Mexico’s recovery picked up in early 2022, but inflation rose sharply and growth was expected to slow.
   - Period fit: excellent for inherited macro conditions in 2022.
   - Ruler attribution: indirect national context, not personal credit/blame.
   - Limitations: macroeconomics only.
   - Contrary points: IMF also notes prudent fiscal/monetary frameworks, so it is not purely negative.

6. [Mexican president's contentious electricity overhaul defeated in Congress](https://www.investing.com/news/commodities-news/mexican-lawmakers-to-vote-on-presidents-contentious-electricity-overhaul-2804968) | Reuters | 17 April 2022  
   - Precise fact: AMLO’s electricity overhaul was defeated in parliament.
   - Period fit: major legislative defeat and evidence of constraint.
   - Ruler attribution: direct, since it was his flagship reform.
   - Limitations: secondary wire report.
   - Contrary points: defeat shows limits of governing coalition, not necessarily absence of agenda-setting power.

7. [El Congreso mexicano rechaza la reforma eléctrica de López Obrador](https://elpais.com/mexico/2022-04-18/la-camara-de-diputados-rechaza-la-reforma-electrica-de-lopez-obrador.html) | EL PAÍS México | 18 April 2022  
   - Precise fact: opposition blocked the constitutional reform; the article describes it as the government’s first major parliamentary defeat.
   - Period fit: strong local-language corroboration of the April reform setback.
   - Ruler attribution: direct.
   - Limitations: editorial framing is more interpretive than Reuters.
   - Contrary points: opposition victory may reflect coalition arithmetic more than a durable governing collapse.

8. [La del INE, crónica de una marcha "de clases medias"...](https://www.eluniversal.com.mx/nacion/la-del-ine-cronica-de-una-marcha-de-clases-medias-y-de-la-que-no-se-sabe-cuantos-asistieron/) | El Universal | 13 November 2022  
   - Precise fact: large demonstrations opposed AMLO’s electoral reform push and defended INE autonomy.
   - Period fit: important for institutional conflict in late 2022.
   - Ruler attribution: direct because the protest targeted his reform.
   - Limitations: crowd-size debates and newspaper framing.
   - Contrary points: protest size alone does not prove legislative or judicial impact.

9. [Mexico: Voices Against Indifference](https://www.article19.org/resources/mexico-voices-against-indifference/) | ARTICLE 19 | 28 March 2023  
   - Precise fact: 696 attacks on the press in 2022; 12 murdered journalists; many attacks involved state actors.
   - Period fit: excellent for 2022 media-freedom and repression context.
   - Ruler attribution: strong but indirect; it captures the environment under AMLO, not a single decree.
   - Limitations: advocacy source; it is not a government dataset.
   - Contrary points: it documents structural violence, not every case as direct presidential action.

10. [Sólo 3 de cada 100 homicidios dolosos se resuelven en el sistema de justicia penal](https://mexicoevalua.org/solo-3-de-cada-100-homicidios-dolosos-se-resuelven-en-el-sistema-de-justicia-penal/) | México Evalúa | 5 October 2022  
    - Precise fact: homicide impunity remained extreme; the report also flags weak certification of Guardia Nacional personnel.
    - Period fit: strong inherited-condition source for justice and security capacity.
    - Ruler attribution: indirect, institutional rather than personal.
    - Limitations: system-level analysis, not AMLO-only.
    - Contrary points: poor outcomes are partly historical and federal-state in origin.

11. [Índice de Estado de Derecho en México 2021-2022](https://worldjusticeproject.mx/en/indice-de-estado-de-derecho-en-mexico-2021-2022/) | World Justice Project México | 23 October 2022  
    - Precise fact: the report says rule-of-law conditions deteriorated in much of Mexico, especially checks, civic space, justice, and anticorruption.
    - Period fit: very strong for Chapters 4B, 7B, and 8B.
    - Ruler attribution: indirect, but useful as independent institutional baseline.
    - Limitations: subnational index, not a ruler study.
    - Contrary points: the report also notes some areas where the system remains stronger than peers.

12. [Cuarto Informe de Gobierno](https://amlo.presidente.gob.mx/cuarto-informe-de-gobierno/) | Presidencia de la República | 1 September 2022  
    - Precise fact: official self-assessment emphasizes pensions, health, infrastructure, energy, and “security, peace, and justice.”
    - Period fit: useful as the government’s own favorable framing for 2022.
    - Ruler attribution: direct.
    - Limitations: promotional self-report, so it should not be treated as independent evidence.
    - Contrary points: it is a useful contrast set against critical and independent sources.

**Compact Event Map**
- **January to March 2022:** persistent journalist killings, pressure on press, and continued insecurity/impunity.
- **10 April 2022:** revocation referendum confirms AMLO remains in office, but turnout is too low to produce a binding mandate.
- **17 April 2022:** electricity reform fails in Congress, marking a major legislative defeat.
- **Mid-2022:** inflation and post-pandemic recovery shape the macro backdrop; government claims stabilization and recovery.
- **9 September 2022:** Guardia Nacional legal changes deepen militarized security governance.
- **November 2022:** large public protests against the electoral reform push show continued institutional conflict around INE autonomy.

**Chapter Source Plan**
- **1B:** IAEA CNPP / NTI nuclear profile for civil nuclear capability context; use only for capability, not responsibility.
- **2B:** INE revocation record, DOF Guardia Nacional decree, Mexico Evalúa, and ARTICLE 19 for security-state and conflict context.
- **3B:** ARTICLE 19, Amnesty, México Evalúa, and local-language press reports for repression, journalist safety, and civil-liberties conflict.
- **4B:** Constitution article 89, INE revocation, El Universal, and WJP for powers, checks, and political constraints.
- **5B:** IMF and the government’s fourth report for macro context, recovery, and policy narrative.
- **6B:** Official health / social-program reporting plus UN/IFI sources when you need welfare context beyond the local prior.
- **7B:** WJP and México Evalúa for corruption, rule-of-law, and impunity context.
- **8B:** WJP, IMF, and the official fourth report for governance-capacity and implementation constraints.

If you want, I can turn this into a tighter evidence dossier format next, or expand any one chapter’s source family into a more detailed source matrix.
